title: Connexions de Gauss-Manin et équations de Picard-Fuchs. Opération de Cartier : copies de tapuscrit annoté (s.d.), tiré à part (1981), notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is section ② of a systematic account of the Cartier operation for F_p-algebras. Section ① on the previous page computed de Rham cohomology for an algebra B/A with a p-base. Here Grothendieck builds the map that becomes the inverse Cartier operator.

(1) He claims there is a unique ring homomorphism ψ: Ω*_{B/A} → Z*_{B/A} (closed forms) with ψ(x) = x^p on Ω^0 = B and ψ(dx) = x^{p-1}dx. As justification he checks only that ∂x := x^{p-1}dx satisfies a Frobenius-twisted Leibniz rule, ∂(xy) = x^p ∂y + y^p ∂x, which is indeed trivial.

(2) Z* is an algebra over Λ = A[B^p]. Through Λ it is also an algebra over the Frobenius twist B̃ = B ⊗_A Ã, where Ã is A viewed over itself via F_A. The relative Frobenius B̃ → B, x⊗a ↦ a x^p, has image exactly Λ. The composite B → B̃ → B is the absolute Frobenius F_B.

(3) ψ is semilinear over B → B̃. It therefore linearises to a map of Λ-algebras ψ̃: Ω*_{B/A} ⊗_B B̃ ≅ Ω*_{B̃/Ã} → Z*_{B/A}. This uses the standard base change of Kähler differentials.

(4) Composing with Z* → H*_DR(B/A) gives the boxed map φ: Ω*_{B̃/Ã} → H*_DR(B/A). This is the inverse Cartier operator C^{-1}.

On the next page Grothendieck proves that φ induces Ω*_{B̃/Ã} ⊗_{B̃} Λ ≅ H*_DR(B/A) when B/A has a p-base, by reduction to one variable plus Künneth. The inverse of this isomorphism is the Cartier operator C. This is the standard Cartier isomorphism in the relative, Frobenius-twisted form that also appears in Katz's 'Nilpotent connections and the monodromy theorem' (1970), §7.
errors: The ring homomorphism ψ: Ω*_{B/A} → Z*_{B/A} with ψ(dx) = x^{p-1}dx does not exist in general. The map x ↦ x^{p-1}dx is not additive as a map to Z^1: (x+y)^{p-1}d(x+y) − x^{p-1}dx − y^{p-1}dy = d(Σ_{0<i<p} p^{-1}binom(p,i) x^i y^{p-i}). This difference is exact but not zero; for p = 2 it equals d(xy).

Grothendieck's check covers only the twisted Leibniz rule and omits additivity. The construction works only after passing to H*_DR = Z*/B*, which is exactly where his boxed map φ lands. So φ is correct, but ψ and ψ̃ with values in Z* are not well defined.
The 'uniqueness' statement is likewise only meaningful for the map into H*_DR.

ideas.what: Frobenius-semilinear map Ω*_{B/A} → H*_DR(B/A) sending x to x^p and dx to the class of x^{p-1}dx (inverse Cartier operator).
ideas.usually_credited_to: P. Cartier (1957); relative form N. Katz (1970)

ideas.what: Linearisation through the Frobenius twist B̃ = B ⊗_{A,F_A} A, whose relative Frobenius has image Λ = A[B^p], giving Ω*_{B̃/Ã} → H*_DR(B/A).
ideas.modern_name: Relative Frobenius and the Frobenius twist B^{(p)}; relative Cartier isomorphism

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, carefully set-up treatment of the Cartier isomorphism for algebras with a p-base, a well-known result. The only notable feature is a small slip: the lift to closed forms is not additive.
